newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea again demands return of sub, crew.
newsitem.headline: North Korea again demands return of sub, crew.

text.p: North Korea on Monday again demanded the return of the bodies of crewmen and the lone survivor from a submarine that ran aground in South Korea in September.

The state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), monitored in Tokyo, said Pyongyang also demanded that South Korea return the vessel itself and apologise for what it called the cold-blooded killing of the crewmen.
"If they (South Korea) persistently refuse to accept our demand, they will be held wholly responsible for the possible consequences," KCNA said.
"We mean what we say...It is the revolutionary spirit of our army and people to do what they determine," KCNA said in a statement.
The submarine, which Seoul says was carrying 26 North Koreans, ran aground on a beach in South Korea on September 18.
KCNA condemned the 50-day manhunt by South Korea's two-million-strong armed forces in which 23 of the North Koreans were killed. The rest were captured or are still missing.
KCNA repeated its claim that the submarine ran aground by accident after suffering engine trouble and the seamen on board did not even have rifles.
"There is a limit to our self-control," KCNA said. "There is no guarantee that the incident, which should be resolved in a peaceful way, will not develop otherwise."
The threat of "possible consequences" over the submarine incident followed a North Korean warning last Friday that it could no longer keep its nuclear programme frozen.
Pyongyang said the United States was not living up to promises it made to persuade North Korea to drop a nuclear programme suspected of developing atomic weapons.
The two Koreas technically remain at war since the 1950-53 Korean War ended in a truce rather than a peace agreement.
